Latest CAS, or I fetch it
Loan statement, or just the EMI

screens.title: Family circle
screens.purpose: Who the plan is for. The entry screen for both paths; dependants drive protection, children's ages drive education goals.

Name, age, earns yes or no; tap to edit
Age; lives with you yes or no
Yes or no; adds a recurring expense line inside Fixed on D06b

Prefilled from R02 household type (spec v0.1).
Each child suggests an education goal on D07; each dependant raises the term-cover need in G05 (spec v0.1).
Just me sets members to you only and has_dependants to explicit none (rule 6).
Pets card (row 8 note): yes or no; feeds a recurring expense line inside Fixed on D06b.
states: Just me: partner, kids and parent cards collapse
Family is always typed; AA has nothing to prefill here
Exit (rule 12): autosave, then O03

screens.title: Your investments, by type
screens.purpose: The overview list for what you own: one row per type with its status and source tag. Both paths pass through it.
ui: Now what you own. One type at a time; approximate is fine, I mark it so.
AA-fed Rs 8.2 L; edit or add
AA-fed Rs 11.8 L; edit or add
Running total so far: Rs ___ against the Rs 15 L you guessed earlier (R04)

logic: Overview list (rule 2): one row per type with its status (value, none, not sure, not asked yet) and its source tag; AA-fed rows show the value and edit or add.
Continue walks the ten type screens in order; a row opens its screen directly.
Plausibility (rule 4): the running total against the R04 corpus band; a mismatch prompts a check, never a block.
Gate fields in this section: bank_and_deposits, mutual_funds, stocks, epf (appendix B); the rest sharpen the plan.

Branch B (4.2): an unknown gate item maps to the R04 corpus band split by the L02 default mix, tagged assumed with a verify action in the plan; to be verified: the default asset mix for unknown splits.

screens.purpose: Every loan as a list; EMI exact, outstanding and years left as bands, rate derived. Feeds the EMI burden, the prepay verdict and term cover.

EMI exact; outstanding and years left as bands; rate derived: about N percent, correct it if you know it
EMI exact; outstanding and years left as bands; rate derived
EMI exact; outstanding and years left as bands; rate derived

Home loan flagged tax-deductible on D03a; effective rate = rate x (1 - tax bracket); prepay verdict per the React debt logic (spec v0.1).
No loans sets has_loans to explicit none and total_emi to zero as a value, not a not-sure (rule 6).
Loan detail (D03a) holds lender, the tax-deductible flag and whether prepayment is allowed (row 59).
states: Loans are not reliably on AA yet; manual (spec v0.1)

screens.purpose: What is protected today, as a list. Three answers per policy type; only the first opens an amount screen.

Have it and know the amount
Have it, not sure of the amount
Have it and know the amount
Have it, not sure of the amount

logic: Per policy type three chips (rule 6): Have it and know the amount opens the amount screen (D04a, D04b); Have it, not sure of the amount sets the amount to not sure and offers the ladder (the policy schedule PDF to the Vault; the premium from the bank debit); Do not have it sets explicit none.
Blindspot and concern copy fires on explicit none only; not sure produces a verify action on G05 and H04 (rule 6).
Term cover need uses the React formula (spec v0.1). Employer-only health cover triggers the health advice per the React; thresholds from L02 (spec v0.1).
Additional screens per policy type (row 60): D04a term, D04b health, D04c other.

screens.title: How the month ends
screens.purpose: The V5 end-of-month pattern, four options, one tap.
ui: Honestly - how does the month typically end?
I have a meaningful surplus - I'm actively deciding where it goes
I'm roughly break-even - income and spending are well matched
It varies - some months surplus, some months tight
I'm often short - the month runs out before the salary arrives

logic: V5 Q1.4, four options verbatim; a tap auto-advances (rule 2).
Feeds the expenses micro-feedback (D12d) and the cashflow concern when the month is often short (V5 4.3).
A check against D06a: often short with a large surplus prompts a look at the outgoings number, never a block (rule 4).

screens.title: Goals and key life events
screens.purpose: Where we are heading and what is coming along the way. Suggested from the family circle; the user edits, adds, ranks.
ui: Last one, and the most important. Everything so far tells me where you are. This tells me where we are heading.
Name, year, cost today, priority; tap to edit
Work-optional age: 60 by default, change it
Yes list: things you want to say yes to, in your words

fields.note: at least one goal or explicit none

logic: Gate (appendix B): at least one goal or explicit none (No goals for now), plus work_optional_age.
Suggested goals come from D01: each child an education goal (spec v0.1).
Retirement is not mandatory; work-optional age is an anchor assumption with its own screen D07b, default 60 (spec v0.1; Vatsal, 10 Sep 2026).
Goal types match the React key-life-events categories: education, home, vehicle, wedding, health, plus travel, business, parents, other (spec v0.1).
No cap on goals; priority order feeds the SIP reconciliation when surplus is short (M4 stage 7) (spec v0.1).
A goal with no timeline or budget is stored as-is, excluded from the SIP maths and shown on the Yes list only (M2 6.1).
states: No goals: the plan covers emergency fund, protection, cashflow, debt and the work-optional projection (spec v0.1)
Exit (rule 12): autosave, then O03
